MAJOR: hil:<actor> validation method is unspecified: design requires the field but does not say it is verified against an authenticated identity/allowlist, so any operator could self-assert HIL confirmation and satisfy the guard at the new endpoint.

AC-2 requires the delta reason to cite the latest review SHA, but FR-2/design_pack contracts only list "refuse unreviewed/non-ancestor" and omit the reason-citation rule, leaving the AC-2 half of validation unimplemented/tested by design.

New network endpoint contract (guardrail 8/9) states no tenant/subject scoping for /items/{id}/decisions; with only "operator role" authz, item-ID enumeration could cross scope — design must declare scoping or explicitly assert single-tenant.
Design pack does not answer the design-guardrail checklist (CL-008): availability/defence-in-depth, observability depth, and invariant ordering are absent; only rollback and tests are addressed.
MINOR: Rollback claims "code revert only / no data migration", but append-only decisions written via the new route persist after revert with no purge/statement of post-rollback handling.
Observability is limited to "API errors and budget output": no structured log/metric for decision appends, HIL rejections, or budget refusals (guardrail 10).
Append ordering/sequence invariant is not stated (append-only yes, but ordering and duplicate-POST behavior beyond the revision guard is undefined).
Failure matrix defines only VALIDATION_FAILED while FR-1 declares 400/404/409; error-code contract is not aligned across design_pack and functional spec.
Language-rule classification of the new route (new shipped logic vs. edit to shipped Python in api/routers/backlog.py) should be explicitly asserted in the design.
NIT: FR-3 test only asserts route existence in OpenAPI; a contract snapshot/diff would catch schema drift more reliably.
"no added runtime latency" NFR has no stated measurement or threshold.
SUMMARY: Design is directionally sound (operator-only, append-only, revision guard, reviewed-ancestor + ancestor-of-HEAD check, tests with a named failing test), and rollback is code-only with no migration.
Top risks: unspecified HIL actor verification, missing reason-cites-latest-SHA rule in FR-2 contracts, and undefined tenant/subject scoping on the new endpoint — all must be resolved before Gate 1.5.
Guardrail checklist responses (availability, observability, invariants) and error-code contract alignment should be added to the design pack.
